question: Why can a pump have excessive discharge pressure?
expected_points: The suction and/or discharge lines can be closed or blocked.
Excessive pump speed can cause the problem.
The pressure relief valve may fail to open.
The pump should have overpressure protection using relief valves.

question: How can a pump be protected from overpressure?
expected_points: Use relief valves to protect the pump from overpressure.
Provide pump overpressure protection to prevent pump or driver malfunction and rupture of the pump or piping.
Do not set the relief valve higher than the maximum pressure rating of the pump.
The relief valve should be connected in the pump discharge line close to the pump.

question: What can cause a pressure relief valve not to open?
expected_points: Spring tension can be too high.
Foreign particles can be present in the valve.
Pump operating temperature can be too high.

question: What operating factors affect pump performance?
expected_points: Speed
Liquid viscosity
Temperature
Inlet pressure
Discharge pressure
Filtration
Duty cycle
Drive type
Mounting

question: What are the requirements for the pump suction line?
expected_points: Pump inlet pressure should be greater than or equal to the minimum required pump inlet pressure (NPIPR).
The suction line should be as short as possible.
The suction line diameter should be equal to or larger than the pump inlet size.
All suction-line joints must be tight and sealed.
A foot valve or liquid trap should prevent the suction line from draining when required.

question: What can cause abnormal pump vibration?
expected_points: Misalignment
Restricted suction line
Air in system
Dirty suction strainer
Relief valve chatter or leakage
Heavy internal rubbing of pump parts
Mechanical problems
